title: Characterization of tumor-specific human endogenous retroviruses in clear cell Renal Cell Carcinoma
text:
Despite frequent reports that human endogenous retroviruses (HERVs) are up regulated in clear cell Renal
Cell Carcinoma (ccRCC), their precise role in cancer development, progression, and treatment has not been
thoroughly investigated. Understanding the relationship between HERV expression in tumors and anti-tumor
adaptive immune responses could yield important insights on the design or enhancement of immunotherapies.
This project seeks to characterize HERV expression in ccRCC to identify potential tumor-specific antigens and
evaluate their immunogenic properties, with the aim of discovering novel therapeutic targets for ccRCC and
advancing HERV research in other cancers.

title: Array-Based Innervated salivary gland microphysiologic system
text:
Many organs in the body are highly innervated which critical for normal function. Incorporating nerves into in
vitro tissue culture systems has been overlooked. This project will demonstrate a microphysiologic system
(MPS) that promotes the maturation of similar size innervated salivary gland tissue mimetics (iSGm) cultured in
an array format for use in high-content toxicity testing and drug discovery.

title: Clonal hematopoiesis, mild cognitive impairment and kidney function decline
text:
The current application seeks to identify and understand the role of DNA changes in blood cells in the
development of new onset mild cognitive impairment, dementia and kidney disease progression. Strong
epidemiologic evidence indicates that chronic kidney disease (CKD), an age-related clinical disorder is
associated with accelerated cognitive function decline. Knowledge gained from this work may contribute to the
discovery of new ways to reduce the burden of cognitive function decline and kidney disease progression
associated with aging.

title: Aging Impairs Wound Healing by an HSC-Autonomous Mechanism
text:
Tissue repair is critical for the survival of all organisms and aging causes a gradual decline of
tissue integrity due to decreased stem cell function, a major hallmark of aging. We will show
that aging impairs wound healing by its effects on blood Stem cells called hematopoietic stem
cells. We can restore youthful wound healing in aged mice by restoring normal hematopoietic
stem cell function.

title: Machine learning approaches for the discovery, repurposing, and optimization of natural products with therapeutic potential
text:
Natural products from bacteria, fungi, and plants have long been a rich source of therapeutically
relevant molecules, but the relationship between natural product structure and activity is not fully
understood, hindering our ability to further optimize natural products for therapeutic use.
Machine learning can be used to develop models that explain trends in data and make
predictions for new data points. In this work we will apply machine learning to understand
structure-activity relationships in natural products, design biosynthetic gene clusters to improve
our ability to biosynthesize natural product analogs, and repurpose natural products as protein-
protein interaction inhibitors.

title: Advancing immunotherapy through cross species studies of immune cell responses and immune checkpoint inhibitor effects in dogs and humans with invasive urinary bladder cancer
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because greatly expanding the applicability
of the canine invasive bladder cancer model, especially related to improving immunotherapy,
will propel success in more fully understanding and effectively treating cancer in humans. This
will impact NIH's mission toward human health by subsequently increasing the number of
successes and limiting the number of failures in human clinical trials, thus ultimately preventing
suffering, saving lives, and reducing health care costs of bladder cancer. The proof-of-concept
work will also justify the identification of other naturally-occurring dog cancer models to improve
therapy for other cancers.

title: Optimizing Recovery prediction after Cardiac Arrest (ORCA)
text:
Physicians’ struggle to accurately distinguish patients who will awaken from coma after cardiac arrest from
those with irrecoverable injury. This proposal brings together a diverse team of world-class experts in post-
arrest care, statistical modeling and machine learning to develop a tool that rapidly and accurately delivers
prognostic information to doctors. Improving the speed and accuracy of post-arrest prognostication will save
lives, allow appropriate resources to be directed to patients who are likely to benefit, avoid long and difficult
care for patients who cannot recover, and spare families the agony of prolonged uncertainty.

title: Expanding single-cell transcriptomics to chart the role of noncoding RNAs in normal hematopoiesis
text:
Noncoding RNAs are emerging regulators of normal hematopoiesis, affecting hematopoietic self-renewal,
function, and lineage commitment. While single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) has enabled the precise study
of individual hematopoietic gene expression programs, our ability to analyze how noncoding (nc)RNAs bias and
commit cells toward hematopoietic fates has been hampered by the fact that scRNAseq only profiles
endogenously polyadenylated RNAs such as messenger (m)RNAs, which excludes most ncRNAs. In this
proposal, I will focus on developing methods and a computational pipeline for single-cell “total” (mRNA + ncRNA)
RNAseq (scTRS), applying these methods to mobilized peripheral blood cells from healthy individuals, and
identifying and validating candidate transfer RNA and long ncRNA drivers of hematopoiesis to provide our first
comprehensive, single-cell examination of how ncRNAs drive normal hematopoiesis.

title: Uncovering Nonlinear Genetic Architectures in Alzheimer's Disease Cellular Pathogenesis
text:
This research develops new statistical and computational tools to uncover genetic effects in Alzheimer's dis-
ease that standard analyses often miss, including interactions and effects that occur only in speciﬁc brain cell
states or at the extremes of molecular measurements. By integrating genomics and multi-omics data with
distribution-aware methods, the project aims to generate a public atlas and software that improve genetic risk
assessment and accelerate the discovery of therapeutic targets. The resulting resources will support more pre-
cise prevention and treatment strategies for people at risk for Alzheimer's disease.

title: Mass Spectrometry
text: Mass Spectrometry Core (formerly Metabolomics Core) Diabetes and its related endocrine and metabolic disorders are characterized by disruption of homeostasis. Aberrant signaling cascades involving protein post translational modifications such as phosphorylation, accumulation of potentially toxic lipid species, and altered flux of intracellular metabolites are among the abnormalities that constitute the diabetic milieu. The DRC Mass Spectrometry Core, an expanded version of the former Metabolomics Core, provides rigorous mass spectrometry-based proteomics and metabolomics analyses to DRC investigators that include quantification, structural characterization, and functional characterization of diabetes-related biomolecules. The Core increases efficiency and cost effectiveness by providing centralized, standardized mass spectrometry analyses to study molecular mechanisms of the pathogenesis of diabetes, its risk factors, and its complications. A major goal of the core is to promote use of mass spectrometry (MS) methods in diabetes research through training, collaboration, development, service, and dissemination. Specific objectives of the Core are: 1) to provide and maintain functional MS systems for diabetes-related studies; 2) to consult with DRC investigators regarding how MS can advance their research programs; 3) to perform service-related MS analyses for diabetes investigators, such as quantifying target analytes, obtaining spectra for structural identification, and assisting with mass spectra interpretation; 4) to develop new MS methods; and 5) to provide training to students and fellows in principles and use of MS systems. During this past funding period, this Core, operating as the Metabolomics Core, provided services to 34 different DRC member laboratories, including 3 P&F recipients, and the >11,000 hours of Core service supported the publication of 90 papers. Through a substantial institutional investment, the capabilities of this Core have increased prompting a name change to DRC Mass Spectrometry Core. The services offered by the Mass Spectrometry Core reflect the evolving bioanalytical needs of DRC investigators, including 1) quantitative study of protein expression, including targeted assays from clinical samples; 2) quantitative assessment of protein-protein interactions; 3) characterization of post translational modifications; 4) elucidation of the biological functions of proteins or protein groups; 5) targeted metabolomic services; 6) broad surveys of multiple metabolic pathways and quantification of pathway metabolites via untargeted metabolomics; and 7) high-throughput, quality-controlled measurements of analytes in large sample sets from clinical studies. The Mass Spectrometry Core thus leverages substantial institutional investments in instrumentation and analytical expertise to promote new discoveries and scientific progress in diabetes research at the Washington University DRC.

title: The Genetic Basis of Variation in Post-Transcriptional Regulation of Stress Defense
text:
Proper regulation of stress defenses is a feature of healthy cells and organisms, and defects in stress defense
are connected to a number of human disorders. This proposal will take advantage of natural variation in stress
signaling in yeast to explore why certain individuals are more susceptible or resilient to stress, with a focus on
less well understood post-transcriptional and post-translational modes of regulation. The results will provide a
strong foundation of understanding how regulatory variation can impact stress responses important for human
health.

title: Chemical glycobiology tool development: Proximity-based modalities
text:
This project focuses on the design and construction of bifunctional molecules that bring 
extracellular proteins into proximity with cell-surface receptors, leading to a new biological 
outcome that could treat human disease. This advancement can lead to new types of treatments 
for cancer and autoimmune diseases.

title: SoS: BIO: Improving the Integrity of Harms Reporting in Biomedical Research: A Science-of-Science Framework for Measurement, Causality, and Intervention
text:
RELEVANCE {See instructions):
The proposed project addresses a central weakness in the biomedical evidence ecosystem: the
incomplete, inconsistent, and sometimes misleading reporting of harms in clinical trials. These
deficiencies compromise the validity of systematic reviews, misinform regulatory and clinical
decision-making, and erode public trust in science. While prior research has documented discrepancies

title: Cellular and Molecular Mechanisms of Dermal Condensate Formation
text:
Understanding the regulation of dermal condensate formation during hair follicle morphogenesis is a crucial
requirement for future hair regenerative therapies. We will systematically define the functional and mechanistic
role axonal guidance signaling pathways play in the directional migration and cellular clustering of the dermal
condensates of nascent hair follicles. This work will expand our knowledge of how the hair-inductive competence
the follicle niche is acquired, which may be useful for the development of hair follicle regeneration approaches.

title: A Deep Learning-based Miniature Microscope for Imaging Aging and Alzheimer's Disease Brains
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it will create a widely accessible tool for understanding age
and Alzheimer’s disease (AD)-related changes to brian function. This research is relevant to the NIH’s mission, and in
particular the mission of NIA because it will transform how scientists can study the brain during aging and AD progression,
generate fundamental knowledge about the neurobiology of circadian rhythms, and pave the way for physician scientists
to test new therapeutics for age-related neuropathologies.

title: Crosstalk of Immune Dysregulation and Impaired Wound Healing in inherited STAT4-mediated Autoinflammatory  Disease
text:
Impaired wound healing, vascular damage, and altered immunoregulation result in a
devastating pediatric syndrome known as disabling pansclerotic morphea. We have uncovered
a role for STAT4 as the genetic etiology underlying this autoinflammatory disease. The studies
in this application will focus on targeting novel mechanisms of inflammation, angiogenesis, and
immune-stromal crosstalk to understand the role of STAT4 in disease progression, in order to
prevent morbidity and mortality associated with disabling pansclerotic morphea.

title: Mechanism of Par1c-mediated AMPA receptor trafficking and synaptic plasticity
text:
The human brain is remarkably unique in its high capacity to learn and adapt to new environments, which has
been attributed to the plasticity of synaptic connections. MARK1, which encodes partitioning defective 1c
(Par1c), is a gene that has human-specific accelerated evolution and is associated with autism spectrum
disorder (ASD) and bipolar disorder, suggesting a role for this protein in learning and memory. This project
aims to describe a molecular mechanism of Par1c-mediated synaptic plasticity and learning through AMPA
receptor trafficking.

title: Homologous recombination deficiency and beyond in pancreatic cancer: evaluating the regulators of response to pembrolizumab and olaparib (POLAR) from the immune and genomic perspectives
text:
Current immunotherapies are ineffective for the vast majority of patients with pancreas cancer, and novel
approaches are needed to harness the role of immunotherapy in this disease. Emerging evidence suggests poly-
ADP ribose polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) can render pancreas cancer immunogenic and improve response to
immune checkpoint blockade in a subgroup of patients with homologous repair deficiency (HRD). An improved
understanding of the tumor genetics and immunologic features that contribute to response and resistance to this
therapeutic combination will guide precision immunogenomic strategies to improve outcomes for patients with
pancreas cancer, including beyond those with HRD.

title: Mechanisms of Prion Spread and Neuronal Toxicity
text:
Prion diseases are rapidly progressive, fatal neurodegenerative disorders caused by prion protein 
aggregates spreading through the brain and spinal cord. We will use directed and unbiased 
proteomics experiments to determine how prions trigger synaptic dysfunction and neuronal 
degeneration in well-characterized, highly reproducible neuronal and animal model systems, as 
well as patient samples. We expect that the proposed studies will elucidate the signaling pathways 
that drive synapse loss in prion disease, and uncover new therapeutic targets.

title: The Role of Ezrin in Schlemm’s Canal Cell Mechanobiology in Glaucoma
text:
Glaucoma is a leading cause of blindness, and all current treatments for glaucoma aim to reduce intraocular
pressure (IOP). However, these treatments remain inadequate, largely because the underlying causes of ocular
hypertension in primary open-angle glaucoma are not well understood. In this project, we will investigate the role
of ezrin, a mechano-responsive protein that links the plasma membrane to the actin cytoskeleton, focusing on
ezrin’s involvement in transcellular pore formation, substrate stiffness mechanotransduction, and modulation of
outflow resistance and IOP.
